topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-211(2), while a broker is employed by (working under) an employing broker, may that broker simultaneously act as an independent broker?
choice_a: No -- an employed broker may not act as an independent broker while so employed, though the broker may later transfer to another employer or to independent status
choice_b: Yes, provided the employing broker consents in writing
choice_c: Yes, but only for transactions outside the employing broker's brokerage
choice_d: Yes, without restriction
explanation: Colo. Rev. Stat. § 12-10-211(2) provides that a broker in the employ of another may not act as an independent broker while so employed, but may transfer employment or move to independent status through the proper notification process.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-211(3), when a licensee's employment is discharged or terminated, in what manner may the required notice to the commission be furnished?
choice_a: Only the broker of record may submit notice, exclusively through the commission's online portal
choice_b: Either party may furnish the notice in a manner acceptable to the commission, but the notifying party must also inform the other party in person or in writing
choice_c: Notice must be submitted jointly on a single form signed by both parties
choice_d: Notice may be given verbally to any commission employee, with no follow-up required
explanation: The statute provides: "Either party may furnish the notice in a manner acceptable to the commission," but the party giving notice must inform the other party of that notice in person or in writing.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-211(4), once a real estate broker's employment has been terminated, may that broker continue performing licensed real estate activities before a new employment record is properly entered by the commission?
choice_a: Yes, for up to 30 days after termination
choice_b: Yes, provided the broker discloses the termination to clients
choice_c: No -- the terminated broker may not perform licensed activities until the commission has entered a proper record of new employment
choice_d: Yes, but only for previously pending transactions
explanation: Under § 12-10-211(4), a broker whose employment has been terminated may not perform licensed activities again until, upon proper notification, the commission enters the change of employment in its records.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(1), fees established under § 12-10-215 are charged for which of the following categories of commission activity?
choice_a: Only original license applications and renewals
choice_b: Only continuing education course approvals
choice_c: Only disciplinary hearing costs
choice_d: Broker examinations, original applications, license renewals, changes of record (such as address), and applications for partnership/LLC/corporation broker status
explanation: Section 12-10-212(1) states that fees established under § 12-10-215 are charged for broker examinations, original applications, renewals, changes of record such as address changes, and applications for partnership, LLC, or corporation broker status.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(2), once an application fee has been submitted to the commission along with a broker application, is that fee refundable if the application is denied or withdrawn?
choice_a: No -- application fees are non-refundable
choice_b: Yes, in full, if the application is withdrawn before review
choice_c: Yes, but only half is refundable
choice_d: Only exam fees are refundable; application fees are not addressed
explanation: Section 12-10-212(2) requires that fees accompany applications and specifies that such application fees are non-refundable.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(3), once a person is issued an individual broker's license, must that broker file further applications or pay additional fees to perform the acts contemplated by that license?
choice_a: Yes, a new application is required for each type of transaction
choice_b: No -- a licensed individual broker may perform all such acts without any further application or additional fees beyond those already specified
choice_c: Yes, an annual supplemental fee is required in addition to the renewal fee
choice_d: Only if the broker changes brokerage firms
explanation: Section 12-10-212(3) grants an individual broker licensee authority to perform all acts contemplated by the license without any further application on his or her part or additional fees beyond those specified in the statute.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(4)(a)(I), apart from the special exception for initial licenses issued in 2018, what is the general renewal deadline for a Colorado broker's license?
choice_a: On or before the anniversary date of issuance, every year
choice_b: On or before June 30 of every third year after issuance
choice_c: On or before December 31 of every third year after the license was issued
choice_d: On or before December 31 of every second year after issuance
explanation: Section 12-10-212(4)(a)(I) sets the general rule that a broker's license must be renewed on or before December 31 of every third year after issuance, with the 2018 initial-license provision being a one-time exception.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(4)(a)(II), renewal of a broker's license is contingent on the licensee providing a written certification of what, and who may establish further renewal procedures by rule?
choice_a: Written certification of net worth, established by the state treasurer
choice_b: Written certification from a supervising attorney, established by the general assembly
choice_c: No certification is required; only the fee payment matters
choice_d: Written certification of completed continuing education for the previous licensing period, with further renewal procedures left to commission rulemaking
explanation: Section 12-10-212(4)(a)(II) conditions renewal on written certification of continuing education completion under § 12-10-213, and authorizes the commission to establish additional renewal procedures by rule.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(4)(a)(IV), the commission has rulemaking authority to do what regarding reinstated licenses?
choice_a: Adopt rules facilitating the transition of reinstatement periods so that reinstated licenses align with the December 31 expiration date
choice_b: Waive all reinstatement fees for licensees over 65
choice_c: Extend the three-year reinstatement window indefinitely by rule
choice_d: Require reinstated licensees to retake the licensing exam by rule
explanation: Section 12-10-212(4)(a)(IV) authorizes the commission to adopt rules facilitating the transition of reinstatement periods to align with the December 31 expiration date scheme.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: A broker's license expired and she later reinstates it by proper application and payment of the required fee. Under § 12-10-212(4)(b), from what date is her reinstated license effective?
choice_a: Retroactively, back to the original expiration date, with no gap in licensure
choice_b: From the date of reinstatement -- it is not retroactive to the original expiration date
choice_c: Retroactively, back to one year before reinstatement
choice_d: From the date the reinstatement application was postmarked, regardless of when it is approved
explanation: Section 12-10-212(4)(b) provides that a reinstated license is effective only from the date of reinstatement; the statute does not restore licensure retroactively to the original expiration date.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-212(4)(c), where are reinstatement fees collected by the commission directed?
choice_a: Directly to the employing broker's trust account
choice_b: To the Colorado general fund
choice_c: To the state treasurer for credit to the division of real estate cash fund
choice_d: To the HOA information and resource center exclusively
explanation: Section 12-10-212(4)(c) routes reinstatement fees to the state treasurer for credit to the division of real estate cash fund, consistent with the general fee-disposition scheme in § 12-10-214.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-214, aside from administrative fines and fees retained by contractors under contract, what happens to all fees collected by the commission under parts 2 and 5 of article 10?
choice_a: They are split evenly among the commission members as compensation
choice_b: They are deposited directly into the state's general fund
choice_c: They are refunded proportionally to all licensees at year's end
choice_d: They must be transferred to the state treasurer for credit to the division of real estate cash fund
explanation: Section 12-10-214 states that all fees collected by the commission under parts 2 and 5, other than administrative fines and contractor-retained fees, are transferred to the state treasurer for credit to the division of real estate cash fund.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-214, besides its standard annual operating appropriation, what may the commission separately request from the division of real estate cash fund?
choice_a: Funding specifically designated for educational and enforcement purposes
choice_b: A discretionary bonus pool for commission members
choice_c: Funding to build additional branch offices
choice_d: A loan to the state general fund
explanation: Section 12-10-214 allows the commission to separately request funding specifically designated for educational and enforcement purposes, in addition to its general operating appropriation.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-214, how must expenditures from the commission's appropriated funds be made?
choice_a: By any method the executive director personally approves, without further documentation
choice_b: Only by vouchers and warrants drawn pursuant to law
choice_c: By direct cash disbursement to licensees
choice_d: By credit card only, per DORA policy
explanation: Section 12-10-214 requires that expenditures be made only by vouchers and warrants drawn pursuant to law.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-215, the fee-adjustment and cash-fund provisions apply to activities of the Division of Real Estate under which parts of article 10?
choice_a: Part 2 only, covering real estate brokers exclusively
choice_b: Parts 1 through 4 only
choice_c: Parts 2, 5, 6, and 7 -- covering more than just real estate brokers
choice_d: All parts of Title 12, covering every regulated profession in Colorado
explanation: Section 12-10-215 states: "This section applies to all activities of the division under parts 2, 5, 6, and 7 of this article 10," so the fee-adjustment scheme covers more than just the broker licensing program in part 2.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-215, the division's proposed annual fee adjustments as part of its budget request must reflect what?
choice_a: The prior year's disciplinary fine revenue only
choice_b: A fixed 3% cost-of-living increase set by statute
choice_c: The average fee charged by neighboring states
choice_d: The direct and indirect costs of administering the programs under the applicable parts of article 10
explanation: Section 12-10-215 requires the division to propose annual fee adjustments reflecting the direct and indirect costs of administering the covered programs.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-215, if the division has unexpended appropriations carried over from a prior fiscal year, what effect does this have on the next year's fee requirements?
choice_a: The carryover becomes part of the next year's appropriation, reducing the fees that need to be collected
choice_b: The carryover must be returned to the general fund and has no effect on fees
choice_c: The carryover triggers an automatic refund to all currently licensed brokers
choice_d: The carryover has no bearing on fee-setting under the statute
explanation: Section 12-10-215 provides that unexpended appropriations from prior fiscal years carry over and become part of the next year's appropriation, correspondingly reducing the fee revenue that needs to be raised.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-215, annual appropriations from the division of real estate cash fund designated as cash funds are subject to what limitation?
choice_a: They are capped at $1 million regardless of fee revenue
choice_b: They shall not exceed the amount anticipated to be raised from fees collected that year
choice_c: There is no statutory limitation on cash fund appropriations
choice_d: They may not exceed the prior year's actual expenditures under any circumstance
explanation: Section 12-10-215 limits annual cash-fund appropriations so that they "shall not exceed the amount anticipated to be raised from fees collected" for that year.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: A broker employed by Employing Broker X decides she wants to move to Employing Broker Y. Under § 12-10-211(2), is this transfer permitted, and what must happen procedurally?
choice_a: No -- once a broker signs with an employing broker, transfer to another employer is prohibited for at least one licensing cycle
choice_b: Yes, but only with the Real Estate Commission's prior written approval of the specific new employer
choice_c: Yes -- the broker may transfer to another employer (or to independent status), but the commission must be properly notified of the change
choice_d: Yes, but the departing broker forfeits her broker's license and must reapply from scratch
explanation: Section 12-10-211(2) permits an employed broker to transfer to another employer or to independent status, subject to proper notification to the commission of the change.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: What is the official statutory heading (catchline) of Colo. Rev. Stat. § 12-10-211?
choice_a: "Continuing education requirements"
choice_b: "License renewal and reinstatement fees"
choice_c: "Disciplinary grounds and investigations"
choice_d: "Change of license status--inactive--cancellation"
explanation: Section 12-10-211 is codified under the heading "Change of license status--inactive--cancellation," reflecting its focus on automatic inactivation triggered by address, employment, and status changes.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under § 12-10-216, what is the maximum period the commission is required to maintain or preserve a licensee's licensing history records?
choice_a: Seven years
choice_b: Three years
choice_c: Ten years
choice_d: There is no maximum; records must be kept permanently
explanation: Section 12-10-216 states: "The commission shall not be required to maintain or preserve licensing history records of any person licensed under the provisions of this part 2 for any period of time longer than seven years."

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under Commission Rule 3.15 (Transition Period License Reinstatement), which brokers are eligible for the transition-period reinstatement provisions described in Rule 3.15.B?
choice_a: Brokers whose license was initially issued on or after January 1, 2018
choice_b: Brokers whose license was initially issued before January 1, 2018
choice_c: Only brokers who currently hold an Inactive license
choice_d: Only brokers who are Employing Brokers
explanation: Rule 3.15.B applies to "a broker whose license was initially issued before January 1, 2018," tying the transition-period reinstatement mechanics to the pre-2018 licensing cycle.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Under Commission Rule 3.11.B.3.a, does the forty-five-day early-renewal window apply only to brokers on Active status, or also to those on Inactive status?
choice_a: It applies only to brokers on Active status
choice_b: It applies only to brokers on Inactive status
choice_c: It applies to all brokers, whether on Active or Inactive status
choice_d: It applies only during the first year after initial licensure
explanation: Rule 3.11.B.3.a states: "All Brokers, whether on Active or Inactive status, may renew their License beginning forty-five (45) days prior to the expiration date of their License," applying the window uniformly regardless of status.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Broker Lee's license expired March 1. He applies for reinstatement on March 25 (within 31 days of expiration) and pays only the regular renewal fee, as § 12-10-212(4)(a)(III)(A) permits. Under § 12-10-212(4)(b), is Lee treated as continuously licensed between March 1 and March 25?
choice_a: Yes -- timely reinstatement within 31 days restores continuous licensure back to March 1 with no gap
choice_b: Yes, but only if Lee can show no transactions occurred during the gap
choice_c: No -- Lee must also pay a reinstatement fee for the gap to be excused
choice_d: No -- even though only the regular renewal fee is owed for a timely reinstatement, the reinstated license is effective only from the reinstatement date, not retroactively to March 1
explanation: Even within the 31-day window where only the regular renewal fee is owed under § 12-10-212(4)(a)(III)(A), § 12-10-212(4)(b) makes the reinstated license effective only as of the reinstatement date -- timely reinstatement avoids the added reinstatement fee, but it does not create retroactive, gap-free licensure.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: Broker Smith is terminated by his employing broker. Smith immediately mails a signed letter to the commission notifying it of the termination but does not separately tell his former employing broker about the notice. Under § 12-10-211(3), has Smith fully complied with his notice obligations?
choice_a: No -- although either party may notify the commission, the notifying party must also inform the other party of the notice, in person or in writing
choice_b: Yes -- notifying the commission alone fully satisfies § 12-10-211(3)
choice_c: No -- only the employing broker, not the individual licensee, may notify the commission under this subsection
choice_d: Yes, as long as the letter was sent by certified mail
explanation: Section 12-10-211(3) requires the party who furnishes notice to the commission to also inform the other party of the notice, in person or in writing; notifying the commission alone does not complete the joint duty imposed by the statute.

topic: License Renewal, Status Changes, and Fees
question: An applicant submits a broker license application with the required fee, but withdraws the application two days later, before the commission has begun reviewing it. Under § 12-10-212(2), is the application fee refunded?
choice_a: Yes, since the commission had not yet begun review
choice_b: No -- application fees are non-refundable regardless of when the application is withdrawn
choice_c: Yes, but only 50% is refunded as an administrative processing fee
choice_d: Refund policy is left entirely to the discretion of the assigned reviewer
explanation: Section 12-10-212(2) makes application fees non-refundable, with no exception for early withdrawal before the commission begins its review.
